before.title: Front Strut-to-Tire Rub Destroying Inner Front Tire Sidewalls
before.description: The 2004-2006 GTO left the factory with marginal clearance between the front strut spring perch and the inner sidewall of the 245-width front tires. The soft factory strut upper mounts/bearings and front radius rod bushings compress and sag early, letting the tire contact the strut body and shave the inner sidewall down to the steel belts — often within 10,000-20,000 miles. NHTSA logged well over 200 complaints across all three model years, including tread separation, highway blowouts, and at least one crash; this front strut rub is a separate defect from the rear-quarter tire rub seen under hard cornering.
before.solution: Replace the front strut upper mounts, bearings, and radius rod bushings (Pedders or Whiteline urethane parts are the accepted fix), install eccentric camber/caster bolts, and realign to gain at least 1/4 inch of tire-to-strut clearance. Inspect inner front sidewalls regularly and replace any tire showing cord; alignment alone without the bushing/mount work rarely cures it.
symptoms: Inner front tire sidewall worn smooth or showing steel cords
Rubbing or scrubbing noise from the front wheels in turns or over bumps
Rubber shavings or dust on the front strut body
Front tires needing replacement every 10,000-20,000 miles
Alignment that will not stay in spec
Front tire blowout or tread separation at speed

before.title: Ignition Lock Cylinder/Housing Binding — Key Will Not Turn
before.description: The ignition lock housing on the 2004-2006 GTO has a locking-pin ramp that wears so the pin no longer rides up when the key is turned, leaving the key stuck in LOCK and the car unable to start; NHTSA electrical-system complaints for all three years describe owners stranded with seized ignitions and locked steering columns. GM developed a revised lock housing with updated material and ramp profile that reuses the existing key barrel, and dealers replaced housings under warranty when the cars were newer. Failures typically begin as intermittent high key effort before the lock seizes completely.
before.solution: Replace the ignition lock housing with the revised-design GM part (the original barrel and key tumblers can be reused, so no re-coding is needed). As a temporary measure, rocking the steering wheel firmly while turning the key, or depressing the lock barrel into the housing, can relieve pin pressure enough to start the car.
symptoms: Key will not rotate out of the LOCK position
Intermittent high effort needed to turn the key before total failure
Steering wheel locked and will not release
Vehicle will not start despite good battery and working remote
Wiggling the steering wheel temporarily frees the key

before.title: Instrument Cluster LCD Odometer Pixel/Display Failure
before.description: The center LCD in the GTO's red instrument cluster (odometer, trip computer) commonly fails: digits lose their lower halves, segments drop out into a 'bar code' pattern, or the display goes fully black while the backlight stays lit. Repair specialists trace it to a failing power-supply circuit on the cluster board — heat-stressed components and cracked solder joints — plus degradation where the LCD ribbon bonds to the board. The failure is especially widespread on 2006 cars and makes the odometer unreadable, which complicates inspections and resale.
before.solution: Send the cluster to an instrument-cluster repair service for LCD replacement and solder re-flow of the power supply circuit, or fit a used cluster ($75-100) and have the mileage professionally reprogrammed to match the car. Simple resoldering fixes intermittent displays in some cases.
symptoms: Odometer digits missing their lower half or random segments
LCD area turns black or blank while cluster backlight still works
Display comes and goes with temperature changes
Odometer/trip display looks like a bar code and is unreadable

before.title: Internal Clutch Slave Cylinder / Throwout Bearing Failure
before.description: The Tremec T56's hydraulic release bearing (concentric slave cylinder, GM part 24264183) sits inside the bellhousing and uses a plastic bearing support that deforms and disintegrates under heat and wear. When the internal seal fails it dumps brake fluid onto the clutch disc, taking out the clutch along with the hydraulics; failures are documented as early as 10,000 miles on otherwise stock cars and appear in NHTSA powertrain complaints. Because the slave is internal, any failure requires full transmission removal to repair.
before.solution: Replace the slave cylinder/release bearing with a fresh GM unit (forum consensus is OEM over aftermarket), and replace it preventively any time the transmission is out for clutch work. Adding a remote bleeder line and an aluminum billet bearing support while in there are widely accepted upgrades.
symptoms: Clutch pedal goes soft or sinks to the floor
Clutch fluid reservoir level dropping with no external leak
Cannot select gears or grinding when shifting with engine running
Chirping or whirring noise when the clutch pedal is depressed
Sudden clutch slip after fluid contaminates the disc

before.title: Rear Differential Mount Bushing Deterioration — Driveline Clunk and Wheel Hop
before.description: The IRS differential on the 2004-2006 GTO hangs from soft rubber mount bushings that deteriorate and allow the diff to rotate under torque. Worn mounts produce a pronounced clunk on throttle tip-in/lift and aggravate the car's notorious axle/wheel hop, which in turn loosens or shears the driveshaft-to-differential bolts and accelerates wear on half-shafts and the crossmember bushings. Differential and driveshaft-bolt failures from this movement appear in NHTSA structural complaints for 2005.
before.solution: Install a polyurethane differential mount insert (Whiteline or Pedders, roughly $40 in parts) to take up the slack in the factory bushing and restore pinion angle; replace the full mount and rear crossmember bushings if badly degraded. Check driveshaft-to-diff bolt torque whenever clunking appears.
symptoms: Clunk from the rear on throttle application or lift-off
Excessive driveline lash or slop shifting gears
Violent wheel hop on hard launches
Driveshaft-to-differential bolts working loose or shearing
Visible differential movement under load

before.title: Rear Shock Upper (Pedestal) Mount Bushing Wear — Rear-End Clunk
before.description: The GTO's rear shocks mount through pedestal-style upper studs with rubber bushings that compress, split, and wear through with age, letting the shock shaft knock directly against the body over bumps. This is one of the most common sources of the GTO's mystery rear-end clunk, alongside the crossmember bushings, and is frequently misdiagnosed; over- or under-torqued upper mounts produce the same noise. The bushings sit behind the trunk/tank trim, so the wear is easy to miss on inspection.
before.solution: Inspect the upper bushings by pulling back the trunk carpet over the tank sides; replace worn bushings with an uprated set (Whiteline W31467 kit, about $34) and torque the upper mount with the car on the ground, top first. If bushings are intact, properly re-torquing the upper and lower mounts cures most shock-sourced clunks.
symptoms: Clunk or thump from the rear over bumps and dips
Noise traceable to the rear shock towers near the trunk
Shock shaft visibly loose or moving at the upper mount
Cracked, flattened, or worn-through upper shock bushings

before.title: GTO LS2 Rear Tire Rub Under Hard Cornering
before.description: 2005-2006 GTO (LS2 6.0L) with the Holden VZ Monaro chassis has limited rear suspension travel and the wide 245/45R17 rear tires can rub the inner fender liner under hard cornering or with two adults in the back seat plus a trunk load. before.solution: Inspect rear inner fender liner for cut marks at each tire rotation. Roll the rear fender lips ($150-$300 specialist) and trim back the plastic splash guard. Avoid maxing out cargo + passengers simultaneously. Aftermarket shorter springs without other geometry changes makes the rub WORSE, not better.
